92043f736e.q: How did Shant Banosian build a billion-dollar mortgage business starting from a $10,000 credit card limit in 2008?
92043f736e.a: Banosian started his retail mortgage office in 2008 during the financial crisis at age 28 with a $10,000 credit card limit. He maxed out and paid off the card repeatedly to fund lead purchases and office furnishings. His first year he closed $9 million in loans, the second year $17 million, and by year three reached $30 million. He expanded from three local towns near Boston into urban markets, then luxury markets, and is now licensed in all 50 states. He progressed from $400 million to over $1 billion annually within three to four years.

b7e60ea059.q: What is Shant Banosian's philosophy on seizing opportunities during market chaos?
b7e60ea059.a: Banosian believes the biggest opportunity for success occurs when there is the most chaos. He estimates that only 5-10% of people figure out that chaos and challenge is where opportunity lies. During the 2008 financial crisis, while 90-95% of his competition was frozen, he positioned himself as having greater leverage and voice. He describes running into the fire when everyone else was retreating, which he credits as the best decision he ever made.

582bf225fd.q: How did LendingTree and LowerMyBills competitive dynamics in the early 2000s prepare Shant Banosian for scaling?
582bf225fd.a: Banosian describes competing against 4-6 other mortgage companies on LendingTree for refinance-only leads, and against 20-30 companies for trigger leads from LowerMyBills. This forced him to differentiate himself, lead on calls, structure his day, and learn how to communicate effectively and separate himself on the phone. He credits these early competitive dynamics from 2003 onward as a gift that taught him essential skills in structure and communication that later enabled his success.
